reading_blocks:
Citrus
HOW TO READ THIS KIT

AN ORANGE ROW IS
A CALL-OUT

Every page is a ranking. Three rows on each are filled solid Citrus orange — those are the call-
outs, and the first is broken out in the panel at the foot of the page: photo, hero numbers, and
the category split behind the projection. Each split is reconciled against the model's own total in
the panel header, so you can check the arithmetic.

PLUS/MINUS IS NOT SCORED — THE PROJECTION
SET CARRIES NO PLUS/MINUS COLUMN.

1
The Pos column is the number that matters
It is the player’s rank inside his own position. A defenceman at D9 taken 52nd overall is a bargain; the same D9
at pick 20 is not.

2
FP/GP separates rate from volume
A high per-game rate on a low games projection is a talent call with a durability discount. A big FPTS total on
82 games is a floor.

3
Tier does not move when you change weights
Tier is fixed under the default scoring. Edit your league’s weights in the workbook and FPTS and both ranks
recalculate — tier stays put as a reference.

4
Blocks are worth a full point
That single weight is why defence rankings here look nothing like a points-only list, and why a shot-blocking
defenceman is the cheapest floor on the board.

5
The call-out panel shows the arithmetic
Each bar is one category: the raw projection times your weight. The longest bar is where that player actually
earns his ranking — and it is a shot or block total more often than a goal total.

These are projections, not predictions, and nothing here claims accuracy against any other system. Projected games played is
availability-adjusted, so a low GP is a durability call, not a data gap. Verify against your own league settings before you draft on it.
